earth_surface.source: NOAA NCEI, Geomagnetism Frequently Asked Questions, https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/products/geomagnetism-frequently-asked-questions
earth_surface.quote: Earth's magnetic field intensity is roughly between 25,000 - 65,000 nT (.25 - .65 gauss).

moon_30km.source: Hood, Torres, Oliveira, Wieczorek & Steward, Lunar Crustal Magnetic Field Map, NASA PDS (2020), doi:10.17189/1520494; file Bm_30km_65S65N_0E360E.tab, column B-Mag (Lunar Prospector + SELENE/Kaguya magnetometer data)
moon_30km.note: 30 km above the mean lunar radius, latitudes 65S-65N, smoothed map; zero cells (no reliable data) excluded. The surface field is not mapped here.

dhiman2023.citation: Dhiman SK, Wu F, Galland P. Effects of weak static magnetic fields on the development of seedlings of Arabidopsis thaliana. Protoplasma 260(3):767-786 (2023; Epub 2022-09-21)
quotes: A field of 50 μT accelerated seed germination by about 20 h relative to samples maintained in a near-null field.
The double mutant, cry1cry2, lacking cryptochromes 1 and 2 displayed the same magnetic field-induced germination acceleration under blue light as the wild-type strain.
Stimulus-response curves for hypocotyl elongation in a range between near-null to 122 μT indicated maxima near 9 and 60 μT for the wild-type strain as well as mutant cry1cry2.
Magnetic field-induced germination acceleration was masked in the presence of exogenous sucrose.
dhiman2023.note: Single study; mechanism unknown (not cryptochrome-dependent). Not used by the model.

gaps_note: No verified measurement is used for these environments in this project.
